transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because my eating habits just went completely off the rails recently. I'm usually pretty strict about tracking my food—you know, macros and all that—but I just stopped caring. I was skipping real meals for days at a time. I basically lived on coffee and protein bars. I didn't even realize how bad it was until I noticed my clothes were just hanging loose on me.
Over the same period when your eating habits changed, how has your mood been? Have you been feeling particularly sad, empty, unusually energetic, or anxious?

Well, my mood has been... really low. Empty, mostly. It all started after a project sponsor at work questioned my judgment. When that happened, it was like... the bottom just completely dropped out. I just sat around my apartment feeling hollow and ashamed. I was even crying over basic work emails—stuff I normally would have just handled without a second thought.
Before this recent episode that started after the work incident, have you ever experienced a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days or stressful weeks before, like anyone, but... never anything like this. I haven't ever had a period where I felt depressed or empty for two weeks straight before this whole work thing happened. This is really the first time it's been like this.
How long have you been feeling this way—this low mood and emptiness—since the work incident happened?

It's been... about three months now. Yeah, three months of just feeling completely hollow and ashamed, not really caring about anything since that whole crisis with the project sponsor. It just hasn't lifted at all.

Before the project sponsor questioned your judgment three months ago, would you say you were functioning well at work and in your personal life? Were you able to handle your responsibilities and enjoy things normally?

Yeah, I think so. Before that happened, everything was... pretty much normal. I was managing my projects fine and getting my work done without any issues. Outside of work, I was doing okay too, just going about my usual routine. I didn't have any trouble handling my responsibilities or enjoying things until that sponsor said what he said.

When your project sponsor questioned your judgment, how would you describe your reaction compared to how you typically handle criticism or setbacks at work? Was this response more intense than you'd normally expect from yourself?

Yeah, it was definitely more intense. Usually, if someone criticizes my work, I just... you know, I take it in, maybe get a little annoyed, and figure out how to fix it. But this time... I don't know, it was like the bottom just completely dropped out. I couldn't brush it off. I ended up just sitting in my apartment for days, feeling completely hollow and... just so ashamed. I was literally sitting there crying over regular work emails that I normally would have just handled without a second thought. It was a complete overreaction compared to my normal self.
Over these three months since the work incident, has your mood been consistently low and hollow the entire time, or have there been days or weeks where you felt somewhat better?

It's been pretty much constant. Ever since that sponsor questioned my judgment, it's just been... like I said, the bottom dropped out. I haven't really had any good days or weeks where it lifted. I just sit in my apartment feeling completely hollow and ashamed, still crying over those regular emails that shouldn't even be a big deal. It's just been this same low feeling the whole time.
Over these three months, how has your sleep been? Are you sleeping more, less, or about the same as you normally do?

I'm definitely sleeping less. It's been pretty bad. Even when I tried to sleep, I just... I kept waking up at weird hours. My mind would go right back to the deployment plan for that project, just stuck on it. And by the time morning came around, I felt completely wrecked instead of rested.
Besides the sleep problems and changes in eating, have you noticed changes in your energy level or ability to concentrate on tasks during these three months?

Well, yeah, my energy is just... it's gone. I don't really have the drive to do much of anything. I haven't wanted to go hiking or edit any of my photos, which I usually love doing. I stopped logging my meals, too. I even have this woodworking project sitting out in my garage, and I haven't even touched it in months. It's strange for me, because doing those things usually helps keep me grounded, but I just... I don't care about any of it right now. I can't focus on them anyway.

Over your lifetime, have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer where your mood was unusually high or energetic, where you needed much less sleep than normal but still felt rested, or where you were more talkative or had racing thoughts?

Yeah, actually, I have. There was a time before all this started where, for days, I just felt almost unstoppable. I felt like my ideas were completely brilliant and I was getting so much done. 

But... it wasn't just feeling good. I was really on edge, too. If someone on my team asked even a basic question, or did anything that slowed me down, I would just snap at them. I remember getting so angry, treating them like they were purposely sabotaging the whole company. I just couldn't handle anyone getting in my way when I was like that.

When you had that period where you felt unstoppable and brilliant with the racing ideas and irritability toward your team—was that before the project sponsor questioned your judgment three months ago, or did it happen around the same time or after?

I'm honestly not entirely sure. It's a little hard to keep the timeline straight in my head right now. I know that energized period happened before this whole rough patch started, but whether it was right before the sponsor made those comments, or... or if it was around the exact same time, I really couldn't tell you. It all just kind of blurs together.

When you think back to that period where you felt unstoppable and brilliant with the racing ideas and irritability—roughly how many weeks or months before the project sponsor questioned your judgment did that happen?

Well, looking back... I guess it was right around the time I was handed some temporary PMO-level responsibilities at work. That whole energized, unstoppable feeling... it built up over about three weeks after I got that assignment. So it was definitely going on before the sponsor made those comments.
